subject: Clarification: SOC 2 audit window and daylight savings impact
messages:
From: Matt O'Leary <matt.oleary@greenbank.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: audits@greenbank.com
Date: 2025-10-09 08:15 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 window question - daylight savings day

Hi Hannah,

Quick question as we prepare evidence for the Type II period: GreenBank's control testing includes a number of point-in-time checks near month boundaries. We noticed Redwood's logging spans timestamps in both PDT and PST around the DST transition in early November. For clarity: if a control owner says "end of day Oct 31" in their evidence notes, do you interpret that as local date end (23:59 in the local timezone where the system is hosted) or do you normalize to UTC cutoffs for audit purposes?

Specifically, for a customer who requests a snapshot that includes Oct 31, 2025, would a log export with timestamps in UTC that show entries up to "2025-11-01T06:59:59Z" be considered inclusive of Oct 31 in US/PST offsets, given DST ended that weekend? Or should we ask for a point-in-time export that explicitly states the timezone used?

Appreciate a short confirmation — we want to avoid any downstream exceptions during testing.

Thanks,
Matt
GreenBank SOC 2 Team
attachments: none

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Matt O'Leary <matt.oleary@greenbank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-09 09:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 window question - daylight savings day

Thanks for raising this, Matt — important one. Short answer: Redwood normalizes all audit evidence exports and snapshots to UTC and documents the UTC cutoff in evidence metadata. That avoids ambiguity around DST shifts.

A bit more detail for your testers:
- Internal control timestamps are stored in UTC in our logging pipeline.
- When we deliver an export labeled "inclusive through Oct 31, 2025 (end-of-day)", the export will include events up to 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z (i.e., inclusive of Oct 31 in UTC terms).
- For customers who need local-time wording in their report, we provide a small metadata file with the export that maps the UTC cutoff to the customer's requested timezone and offset.

If you prefer, we can produce a point-in-time export that explicitly lists the cutoff timestamp in both UTC and PST/PDT. I can also attach a short sample log CSV showing the timestamp format.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: sample export metadata (stub)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, Matt O'Leary <matt.oleary@greenbank.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-09 11:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 window question - daylight savings day

Adding a little operational context from the logs team so your auditors know what to expect.

- We record all log events as ISO8601 UTC (e.g., 2025-11-01T06:59:59Z).
- Our standard "end-of-day inclusive" cutoff for monthly evidence is exactly 00:00:00Z on the following calendar day. For Oct 31 inclusive that becomes 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z.
- When DST transitions occur, the UTC cutoff method remains stable (we do not shift based on local DST).
- For snapshot-based controls where the auditor needs a point-in-time in the customer's local timezone, we will:
  * produce the snapshot in UTC,
  * include a single-line metadata file showing the equivalent local-time cutoff and the timezone identifier (e.g., America/Los_Angeles), and
  * optionally provide a signed bridge letter that states the snapshot cutoff semantics for the testing window.

I've attached a small log sample (redwood_log_sample_20251001.csv) and a bridge letter template (bridge_letter_template.pdf) for your records. If GreenBank wants the bridge letter signed and returned, note the signer is typically our Head of Compliance.

-Neha
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_log_sample_20251001.csv, bridge_letter_template.pdf

From: Matt O'Leary <matt.oleary@greenbank.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-10 11:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 window question - daylight savings day

Thanks Hannah and Neha — that clears it up. For our testing plan we'll ask for the UTC snapshot plus the metadata mapping to America/Los_Angeles. If it's not too much trouble, please have the bridge letter signed and returned; our auditors prefer having the signed attestation when there's any potential timezone ambiguity.

I'll open the GreenBank evidence request ticket and link the files you provided. Expect a DocuSign for the bridge letter next week.

Best,
Matt
GreenBank SOC 2 Team
